**7B.8 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

**Bottom line**
Mixed, but negative-leaning. Srettha did keep some formal commitments, especially by advancing the signature cash-transfer program, sustaining pro-trade rules, and accepting constitutional transfer after removal. But the strongest evidence is that he repeatedly sold the digital-wallet plan in different ways despite sharp fiscal criticism, pressured an independent central bank, and defended an ethically controversial cabinet appointment until the court removed him. I found no clean proof of deliberate concealment of private gain, but there is clear evidence of opportunistic framing and partial reversal under pressure.

**Accepted claims**

1. **Universal handout promise kept alive**
- **Title:** Thailand’s cabinet approves 13.5 billion digital-wallet handout
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** April 23, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007
- **Claim:** Srettha pushed forward the 500 billion baht digital-wallet plan, a universal 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million Thais. This is positive evidence that he followed through on a major campaign promise rather than abandoning it immediately.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8

2. **Partial policy correction**
- **Title:** Thai PM says part of $13 billion digital-wallet stimulus to be in cash
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** September 3, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-part-of-13-billion-digital-wallet-stimulus-to-be-in-cash-3597164
- **Claim:** The government later shifted part of the digital-wallet plan into cash payments. This is the best positive evidence for correction, but it looks more like tactical compromise than a clean admission that the original design was mistaken.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8

3. **Technocratic appointment as a counter-signal**
- **Title:** Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** April 28, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984
- **Claim:** Srettha appointed Pichai Chunhavajira, a former SET chair and Bank of Thailand board member, as finance minister and deputy PM. This is positive evidence that he sometimes staffed key posts with technocratic figures rather than only loyalists.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8, 7B.5

4. **Trade and investment commitments**
- **Title:** Thailand and Sri Lanka sign free trade agreement
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** February 3, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailand-sri-lanka-sign-free-trade-agreement-3291876
- **Claim:** Srettha signed an FTA covering goods, investment, customs procedures, and intellectual property, and urged the private sector to expand trade and investment. That supports a rule-based commercial posture rather than an obviously opportunistic or insincere one.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8

5. **Orderly constitutional exit**
- **Title:** Thai king endorses Paetongtarn Shinawatra as prime minister
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** August 18, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/thai-king-endorses-paetongtarn-shinawatra-as-prime-minister-3576565
- **Claim:** After Srettha’s removal, parliament elected Paetongtarn and the king endorsed her two days later, showing an orderly constitutional transfer rather than extra-constitutional resistance. This is positive evidence that he did not try to subvert formal succession rules.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8, 7B.7, 7B.6

6. **Digital-wallet rollout problems**
- **Title:** Thailand’s flagship $14 billion handout faces snags and criticism
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Yahoo News
- **Date:** August 1, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html
- **Claim:** Reuters reported registration snags, delayed launch timing, and criticism from economists and former central bankers who called the scheme fiscally risky. This weakens the case that Srettha was being candid about tradeoffs or had a stable implementation plan.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8

7. **Pressure on central bank**
- **Title:** Thai central bank holds key rate, defies government calls for cuts
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** April 10, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-central-bank-holds-key-rate-defies-government-calls-for-cuts-3372713
- **Claim:** Reuters reported the Bank of Thailand resisted repeated government calls to lower rates. This is negative evidence that Srettha’s camp was pressuring an independent institution for short-term political advantage rather than respecting technocratic constraints.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7

8. **Doubling down instead of openly correcting**
- **Title:** Thai PM says digital-wallet scheme will spur jobs and manufacturing
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com
- **Date:** July 11, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-digital-wallet-scheme-will-spur-jobs-and-manufacturing-3514879
- **Claim:** After criticism of the handout plan, Srettha re-sold it as a jobs-and-manufacturing stimulus instead of openly acknowledging earlier doubts. That is negative evidence for candor and suggests rhetorical repositioning under pressure.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8

9. **Ethics case and cabinet appointment**
- **Title:** Thai court says PM Srettha violated rules on ethics in cabinet appointment
- **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint
- **Date:** August 14, 2024
- **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/thai-court-says-pm-srettha-violated-rules-on-ethics-in-cabinet-appointment/2222960/
- **Claim:** The Constitutional Court found Srettha violated ethical rules in the Pichit appointment. This is strong negative evidence that he did not keep political commitments and ethical constraints cleanly separated from personal-network politics.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8, 7B.5, 7B.6, 7B.7

10. **Press denial versus contemporaneous arrests**
- **Title:** Thai journalists arrested over news coverage
- **Publisher:** Reuters via Yahoo News
- **Date:** February 13, 2024
- **URL:** https://www.yahoo.com/news/thai-journalists-arrested-news-coverage-054141721.html
- **Claim:** Two journalists were arrested over reporting on anti-royal graffiti, while Srettha publicly said the government was fair on press freedom and that there was no harassment. The arrest and denial together are negative evidence for manipulation of public information and hiding accountability costs.
- **Question IDs:** 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7

**Search gap**
- I did not find direct evidence that Srettha openly admitted hidden tradeoffs in the digital-wallet plan.
- I also did not find direct proof that he deliberately lied about finances, concealed a private payoff, or formally reversed a stated policy for personal enrichment.
- The strongest pattern is political doubling-down, selective re-framing, and pressure on independent institutions, not documented covert self-dealing.
